verses.text: In Iconium, Paul and Barnabas went together into the Jewish synagogue and spoke. A huge number of Jews and Greeks believed.
But the Jews who refused to believe stirred up the Gentiles and turned them against the believers.
Still, Paul and Barnabas stayed a long time, speaking boldly about the Lord. He confirmed the message of his grace by enabling them to do signs and wonders.
The people of the city split into sides: some backed the Jewish leaders, others sided with the apostles.
Then some Gentiles and Jews, along with their leaders, plotted to attack and stone them.
When Paul and Barnabas found out, they escaped to the Lycaonian towns of Lystra and Derbe and the surrounding area.
There they kept sharing the good news.
In Lystra, a man who had never walked sat listening to Paul. He had been unable to use his feet since birth.
Paul looked right at him and saw that the man had faith to be healed.
So Paul called out, “Stand up straight on your feet!” The man jumped up and started walking.
When the crowd saw what Paul had done, they shouted in the Lycaonian language, “The gods have come down to us looking like humans!”
They called Barnabas “Jupiter” and Paul “Mercury,” since Paul did most of the talking.
The priest of Jupiter, whose temple stood just outside the city, brought bulls and flower garlands to the gates. He and the crowd wanted to offer sacrifices.
When Barnabas and Paul heard about it, they tore their clothes and rushed into the crowd, shouting,

“Friends, why are you doing this? We’re human too, just like you! We’ve come with good news: turn away from these empty things and turn to the living God. He made the sky, the earth, the sea, and everything in them.
“In past generations, God let all the nations go their own way.
“Even so, God never left people without a witness. He did good for you, sending rain from the sky and giving you fruitful seasons. He filled you with food and gladness.”
Even after saying all this, they could barely stop the crowd from sacrificing to them.
Then some Jews came from Antioch and Iconium and won the crowd over. They stoned Paul and dragged him outside the city, thinking he was dead.
But as the disciples gathered around him, Paul got up and went back into the city. The next day he left with Barnabas for Derbe.
They shared the good news in that city and made many disciples. Then they returned through Lystra, Iconium, and Antioch,
strengthening the believers and encouraging them to stay firm in the faith. “We must go through many hardships to enter God’s Kingdom,” they told them.
They appointed elders in every church. After praying and fasting, they entrusted the elders to the Lord, whom they had believed.
They traveled through Pisidia and came to Pamphylia.
After sharing the message in Perga, they went down to Attalia.
From there they sailed back to Antioch, where they had first been entrusted to God’s grace for the work they had now completed.
When they arrived, they gathered the church and reported everything God had done through them, including how he had opened the door of faith to the Gentiles.
They stayed with the believers there for a long time.
